items.title: A finite purely inseparable extension makes the reduction of a finite type scheme geometrically reduced
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section on geometrically reduced schemes
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma produces, for a scheme X locally of finite type over k with finitely many irreducible components, a single finite purely inseparable extension k'/k such that the reduction of X_{k'} is geometrically reduced over k' (statement lines 638-642). Three separate inputs are chained: the reduction lets one work with the generic points x_1, ..., x_n and their residue fields K_i; the purely inseparable base change is a homeomorphism, so the local rings of (X_{k'})_{red} at the points over the x_i are exactly the fields (K_i tensor_k k')_{red}; and one algebra lemma produces a single extension making all of them separable at once, after which the generic-point criterion closes the argument (proof lines 646-670). What is not routine is that one extension suffices for all components simultaneously. The claim is H2.
